title: Instrument cleaning, disinfection and single-use files
audience: Mobile nail technicians who carry metal tools, files and buffers from client to client
learningOutcomes: Sort instruments into single-use, cleaned-and-disinfected and discard groups
Carry out the clean, rinse, dry and disinfect sequence for a reusable instrument
Set up a clean station before a client arrives and keep it clean during the visit

instruction.heading: Sorting the kit
instruction.body: Instruments that cannot be cleaned and disinfected to a verified standard are single-use. These include files, buffers and some cuticle items. Reusable metal instruments are cleaned, dried and disinfected after every client. Any instrument that is cracked, pitted or cannot be cleaned is removed from the kit. Cleaning comes first: an instrument with visible debris is not disinfected until it is clean.

instruction.heading: The clean and disinfect sequence
instruction.body: Wipe off debris with a single-use cloth. Wash in warm water with detergent and scrub joints and hinges. Rinse and dry completely. Disinfect with a product approved for instruments, following the label for dilution and contact time. Store the instrument in a clean, closed container. Record the time and the product used. instruction.heading: Clean station and visit
instruction.body: The station is wiped down before the client arrives and again when the visit ends. Clean instruments are kept separate from used items. A used file goes into a closed waste container, not back onto the tray. Gloves are changed when they are torn, contaminated or after touching the client's skin outside the service.

procedure: Lay out single-use items and clean instruments on a clean tray before the client arrives
Use a single-use file or buffer for each client and discard it at the end of the service
After the visit, wipe debris from each reusable instrument with a single-use cloth
Wash, rinse and dry each reusable instrument, then disinfect it for the label contact time
Store the instrument in a closed container and record the cycle

workedExamples.situation: A technician finishes a pedicure and puts the metal cuticle pusher back on the tray without cleaning it, planning to clean the whole kit at home.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is wrong with this practice and what should happen instead?
workedExamples.reasoning: The instrument has been in contact with the client and has not been cleaned or disinfected, so it must not be used again before it is. The technician wipes, washes, dries and disinfects it at the end of the visit and records the cycle. Leaving it for later does not meet the standard.

equipmentAndPpe: Instrument wash, brush and drying cloth
Disinfectant approved for instruments, with the label
Closed storage container for clean instruments
Sharps or sealed waste container for used single-use items

commonErrors.error: Putting used instruments back on the tray without cleaning.
commonErrors.prevention: Clean and disinfect each reusable instrument after every client.

commonErrors.error: Disinfecting instruments that still have debris on them.
commonErrors.prevention: Clean first, then disinfect with the label contact time.

commonErrors.error: Reusing a file or buffer on a second client.
commonErrors.prevention: Use a new single-use file or buffer for each client.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Disinfectant dilution and contact time follow the product label. UNCONFIRMED: no official source has been fetched for this point in this draft. A reviewer must confirm it before approval.
Sharp or cracked instruments are removed from use and disposed of in a sealed container.

qualityStandard: Each reusable instrument is cleaned, dried and disinfected after every client
Single-use items are used once and discarded in a closed container
The clean-station check is recorded for each visit
documentationEvidence: Instrument cleaning and disinfection log per visit
Record of discarded instruments and reason
Product label or safety data sheet for the disinfectant in use
summary: Single-use items are used once for each client
Reusable instruments are cleaned, then disinfected for the label contact time
Clean and used items are kept separate at every visit

knowledgeChecks.question: When should a reusable metal cuticle pusher be cleaned and disinfected?
options: At the end of the day

knowledgeChecks.question: An instrument has visible debris on it. What is the correct order?
options: Clean and dry it, then disinfect it
